claim: For the complete bipartite graph \(K_{3,3}\), the Morse complex \(\mathcal M(K_{3,3})\) of acyclic discrete vector fields is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of exactly \(80\) four-spheres: \(\mathcal M(K_{3,3})\simeq\bigvee^{80}S^4\).

correctness.rationale: The graph-to-rooted-forest model is the graph specialization of acyclic discrete vector fields. All 3^9 edge states are exhaustively classified. The resulting face vector is independently reproduced by det(lambda I+L)=lambda(lambda+6)(lambda+3)^4. A complete 855-pair matching on all 1791 nonempty faces is checked against all 6894 Hasse covers, and the reversed Hasse orientation is acyclic. Its critical profile is exactly one dimension-0 face and eighty dimension-4 faces. Forman's theorem then gives a CW model with exactly those cells, hence a wedge of eighty 4-spheres. Independent mod-2 boundary elimination gives reduced Betti numbers (0,0,0,0,80).

value.rationale: \(K_{3,3}\) is the smallest balanced complete bipartite graph beyond the star and \(K_{2,n}\) regimes and sits directly inside an explicit literature gap about complete-bipartite Morse complexes. An exact homotopy type is substantially stronger than the known connectivity bound. The result is a natural benchmark for any future formula for \(\mathcal M(\(K_{p,q}\))\), and the 80-sphere decomposition supplies a reusable exact test case rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
